info.title: OpenAsy SAST API
info.summary: Static analysis findings from every pull request; only what is new blocks it.
info.description:
Every screen of sast uses this API, and so can your scripts and CI (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Send SARIF 2.1.0 from any analyser with `SAST_INGEST_TOKEN`. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

post.description:
Takes a SARIF 2.1.0 log from any analyser, such as Opengrep, Semgrep or CodeQL, and compares it with the default branch. Scans of the default branch become the baseline; every other scan reports only the findings the baseline does not have and nobody has triaged, and `blocking` counts those at or above the repository's `failOn`. The repository is created by its first scan.

```bash
opengrep scan --sarif-output=results.sarif .
curl -sf -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SAST_INGEST_TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @results.sarif \
  "https://sast.example.com/api/v1/scans?repository=acme/web&branch=$BRANCH&commit=$SHA&pullRequest=$PR" | tee scan.json
test "$(jq .passed scan.json)" = true
```

The body may be gzipped (`Content-Encoding: gzip`), up to 64 MiB unpacked, with at most 50,000 results.

Takes SAST_INGEST_TOKEN, or an API token with the editor role.

parameters.name: pullRequest
parameters.description: The pull request number or name. A scan of the default branch with a pull request is still compared, not made the baseline.

parameters.name: defaultBranch
parameters.description: Set when the repository is new or the default branch changed. Without it a new repository uses `main`.

201.description: Compared with the baseline. `passed` says whether the check passes.

200.description: The scan and what it found that was new.

patch.description:
Sets the default branch whose scans are the baseline, and the severity that fails a check.

Needs the admin role.

delete.description:
Deletes its scans, findings and triage.

Needs the admin role.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `open` (default): reported on the default branch and not triaged. `suppressed`: triaged and still reported. `resolved`: no longer reported.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches the rule, path or message.

put.description:
Marks a finding as a false positive or accepted risk, with a reason, or opens it again. The decision follows the fingerprint to every branch, so a pull request that adds the same finding does not fail. A finding that is only in a pull request can be triaged too.

Needs the editor role.

parameters.description: From a finding or a scan.

Metrics in the Prometheus text format.

post.description:
The token is checked with GitHub, then sealed with openasy-kek. The account's repositories are listed at once. 503 without openasy-kek.

Needs the owner role.

delete.description:
Its repositories keep their findings, sent from CI from now on.

Needs the owner role.

post.description:
Instead of waiting for SAST_POLL_MINUTES.

Needs the admin role.

put.description:
Git repositories of Opengrep rules that sast-agent fetches at each scan, next to the rules it ships.

Needs the admin role.

get.description:
The last 200, newest first.

Needs the viewer role.

post.description:
Queues a scan of the default branch's last commit, for a repository from a connection.

Needs the editor role.

post.summary: sast-agent: enrol with a one-time token

200.description: At most one job, leased for 30 minutes.
Kept as a scan of the default branch.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when sast runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the sast origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_sast_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when sast is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

ingestToken.description: `SAST_INGEST_TOKEN`: for CI. It can send scans, nothing else.

agentSecret.description: A sast-agent's own secret (`osa_...`), from enrolment.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

FailOn.description: The lowest severity of a new finding that fails the check; `none` never fails it.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

suppressed.description: Open findings someone marked as a false positive or accepted risk.

failingChecks.description: Scans of the last 7 days that failed their check.

source.description: github: from a connection, scanned by sast-agent. ci: sent from CI.

scanEnabled.description: Whether sast-agent scans it when its default branch moves.

headCommit.description: The default branch's last commit, as the forge said.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

active.description: False once the acceptance has expired; the finding is open again.

fingerprint.description: Stable across moved lines and other branches.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

expiresAt.description: Required for accepted, at most 366 days away; optional for a false positive.

kind.description: `baseline` for the default branch, `change` for any other branch or a pull request.

new.description: Findings the baseline does not have and nobody has triaged.

blocking.description: New findings at or above failOn. Always 0 for a scan of the default branch, which adopts what is there.

findings.description: The new findings, most severe first, up to 100.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

account.description: The organization or user whose repositories are scanned.

syncedAt.description: The last time its repositories were listed.

error.description: Why the last listing failed, or null.

token.description: A GitHub token that reads the account's code: a fine-grained token with Contents and Metadata read. Kept sealed, never returned.

ruleSources.description: https addresses of git repositories with Opengrep rules, run next to the shipped rules. Their licence is the install's to check.

enrollToken.description: One-time, for 7 days: SAST_ENROLL_TOKEN on the agent. Shown once.

secret.description: The agent's own secret, kept in its state volume.

token.description: Reads the repository for the clone.
